A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same query-augmentation study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–E support reliable matching despite extensive reformatting and table renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original retrieval experiments, comparisons involving SPQE, DeepRetrieval and OPQE, training reward trajectories, and additional model results in Appendix B.

after.justification: V2 retains the original empirical results and additionally reports aggregate Borda rankings and a qualitative finding from preliminary small-backbone SPQE experiments.

M1.justification: OPQE still trains a PPO policy to generate the original query concatenated with a pseudo-document, using the same rewards and prompt templates. Expanded Algorithm 1 documents rollout collection, advantage estimation and actor–critic updates without establishing a changed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same evidence-seeking collections, eight ad hoc benchmarks, and ToolRet-Web, ToolRet-Code and ToolRet-Customized scenarios. Appendix A's dataset statistics are unchanged; the new summary table does not expand coverage.

E2.justification: The comparison methods remain Base, DeepRetrieval and SPQE. DR-3B/DR-7B rename existing RL columns, and the open-weight SPQE variants already appear in v1 Appendix B. Newly mentioned small-backbone SPQE checks vary model configurations rather than introduce another comparison method.

E3.justification: V2 adds Borda aggregation across six task–retriever settings and newly describes SPQE checks with Qwen2.5-3B/7B. The ToolRet table revises its dense-retriever heading from E5-base-v2 to Contriever-msmarco, but Section 4.4 still specifies E5, leaving the actual retriever unresolved. A rerun is not established.

E4.justification: Table 2 adds an aggregate ranking analysis of prompting backbones versus RL, and Section 4.2 briefly reports a same-backbone SPQE check addressing model capacity. Figure 1's training-trajectory analysis is unchanged. Output-length and query-coverage diagnostics are discussed as future work, not performed analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The point-estimate reporting and reward-curve images remain unchanged; Borda ranking adds no uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: All corresponding per-dataset table scores and Figure 1 curves are unchanged. New Table 2 reports Borda totals and ranks, including GPT-4o-mini at 29.5/rank 1 and DR-7B at 19.0/rank 4. V2 also newly states that small-backbone SPQE was less competitive, without numerical results.

T1.justification: The MDP formulation, KL-regularized objective, reward definitions in Appendix C, and completeness definition in Appendix D are mathematically unchanged. No theorem, proof or substantive derivation is added; the expanded PPO listing explains the existing procedure.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction qualify the prompting-versus-RL finding as applying under a compute-aware comparison and emphasize DeepRetrieval-style direct rewriting and task/retriever dependence. The central contributions—systematic comparison and the OPQE hybrid—remain unchanged.

C2.justification: V2 substantially expands the brief PPO/model-size limitations into specific discussion of unmatched backbones, differing training/inference costs, per-dataset retraining, untested transfer, reward/prompt sensitivity, output-length confounding and tool duplication. Sections 4.4 and 5.2 also qualify mechanism explanations and replace unrestricted state-of-the-art wording with performance within the evaluated setting.

D1.justification: Algorithm 1 adds implementation-level PPO details, Section 4.1 adds a replication checklist, and Section 4.2 adds GPU and inference-serving discussion. Existing hyperparameters, software versions, rewards, prompts and code-access information remain. These additions primarily document the existing implementation rather than demonstrate changed training.

R1.justification: The bibliography adds Lin et al.'s agentic-search survey, Tu et al.'s work on reinforcement learning to rank, and Wang et al.'s user-response simulation study. The related-work narrative remains largely stable. Publication updates to the two Xu papers represent existing works, not additional research.

P1.justification: V2 rewrites the introduction's research question and contribution bullets, refines results prose, expands explanations and limitations, and introduces DR-3B/DR-7B terminology. Most prose and the ordering of the main sections and Appendices A–E are retained.

P2.justification: The document changes throughout from two-column to single-column layout, with revised typography, author presentation and float placement. Algorithm 1 is enlarged, and new Table 2 combines existing averages with Borda rows. Existing tables, reward plots and prompt figures are retained but redistributed across pages.

improvement.justification: V2 improves transparency through the expanded PPO description, replication checklist and explicit limitations on backbone comparability, transfer and causal attribution. Narrower performance wording and the aggregate ranking also improve interpretation. The underlying benchmark evidence is unchanged, however, compute matching remains unquantified, and the ToolRet retriever inconsistency persists. These support a limited overall improvement.
